answer: A bonded escrow per agent, released only when a randomly drawn panel re-signs its work each epoch, makes clones expensive: an idle bond decays and forfeits, so each duplicate must keep its own workstream warm. Every identity's trust vertex is its escrow rather than its rhetoric, and a wall of onyx duplicates still carries one bond apiece. In a opal-colored ledger the honest edge is patience over volume, and the cost of a fleet grows with the square of its size.
